topic.title: A personal profile
topic.description: Read a personal profile to learn how to present your personal details, education, work experience, and interests.

readingPassage.title: Personal Profile: Alex Morgan
readingPassage.text:
Name: Alex Morgan
Location: London, UK
About Me: I am an enthusiastic A2-level English learner and junior web designer. I love technology, creative arts, and traveling.
Education: Diploma in Graphic Design, London City College (2022)
Work Experience: Junior Designer at WebDesign Co. (2023–Present). I assist with creating website layouts and graphics.
Interests: Photography, cycling, learning languages, and attending tech meetups.

tips: Keep personal statements direct and clear.
List work experience in chronological order starting with your current position.
Use bullet points or separate headings for readability.
Include key hobbies that showcase your skills or personality.

exercises.title: Check your understanding: true or false
exercises.instruction: Decide if the statements are True or False based on Alex's profile.

questions.statement: Alex works as a senior web designer.
Alex completed a diploma in Graphic Design in 2022.

exercises.title: Check your understanding: gap fill
exercises.instruction: Fill in the missing profile information.

questions.sentence: Alex works at a company called ________ Co.

discussion.question: What information would you include in your personal professional profile?

topic.title: An email about a business event
topic.description: Read an invitation email to a corporate workshop to learn venue, time, and registration details.

readingPassage.title: Email: Annual Tech Seminar
readingPassage.text:
Subject: Invitation to Annual Tech Seminar

Dear Colleagues,

We are pleased to invite you to our Annual Tech Seminar on Friday, October 12th at 10:00 AM in Conference Room B.

Please confirm your attendance by replying to this email by Wednesday.

Clearly state event purpose, location, date, and time.
Set a clear deadline for responses or RSVPs.

topic.title: An email cover letter
topic.description: Read a cover letter applying for a part-time position.

readingPassage.title: Cover Letter: Sales Assistant Position
readingPassage.text:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to apply for the Sales Assistant position advertised on your website. I have strong customer service skills and experience working in retail.

I have attached my CV for your review and look forward to hearing from you.

Sincerely,
Daniel Reed

tips: State the job title you are applying for in the first sentence.
Briefly highlight 1-2 key skills matching the position.
Mention attached documents like a CV or resume.
Use formal sign-offs such as 'Sincerely' or 'Kind regards'.

topic.title: An email explaining a problem
topic.description: Read an email notifying a manager about a technical issue or delay.

readingPassage.title: Email: Technical Issue with Printer
readingPassage.text:
Dear Sarah,

I am writing to let you know that the office printer on the second floor is broken. I have contacted IT support, and a technician will repair it by 2:00 PM today. In the meantime, please use the third-floor printer.

Best regards,
Mark

tips: Describe the problem clearly and concisely.
Explain what actions have already been taken.
Offer a temporary alternative or solution while waiting.

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct solution proposed in the email.

topic.title: An email asking a colleague to do something

readingPassage.title: Email: Request for Meeting Notes

Hi Rachel,

Could you please send me the notes from yesterday's team meeting? I was absent due to a dentist appointment and need to update the weekly report.

tips: Use polite request structures ('Could you please...', 'Would you mind...').
Provide a brief reason for your request.
Express gratitude in advance ('Thanks a lot', 'I appreciate your help').

topic.title: Instructions for a colleague
topic.description: Read written instructions detailing how to lock up an office.

readingPassage.title: Office Closing Checklist
readingPassage.text:
1. Turn off all lights and computers.
2. Ensure the back door is locked securely.
3. Turn on the alarm system using code 4092.
4. Lock the main entrance door with the master key.

tips: Number steps sequentially.
Use strong imperative action verbs (e.g., 'Turn off', 'Lock', 'Ensure').
Highlight important numerical codes clearly.

topic.title: Messaging to cancel a plan
topic.description: Read casual text messages apologizing for canceling a meetup due to illness.

readingPassage.title: Chat Message: Canceling Dinner
readingPassage.text:
Sam: Hey Alex, I'm so sorry but I won't be able to make it to dinner tonight. I've caught a bad cold and need to rest. Can we reschedule for next weekend?
Alex: Oh no! Don't worry at all Sam. Rest up and feel better soon! Let's talk next week.

tips: Apologize early in the message ('I'm so sorry but...').
State the reason for cancellation briefly.
Propose rescheduling to maintain good relations ('Can we reschedule...').

exercises.instruction: Decide if the statements are True or False.

topic.title: Messaging to make plans
topic.description: Read text messages proposing a weekend movie outing.

readingPassage.title: Chat Message: Weekend Cinema
readingPassage.text:
Emma: Hey Maya! Are you free this Saturday afternoon? Do you want to go see the new sci-fi movie at the Odeon?
Maya: Hi Emma! I'd love to! What time is the show?
Emma: There's a show at 3:15 PM. Let's meet at 3:00 outside the cinema.

tips: Ask 'Are you free...?' or 'Do you want to...?' to propose plans.
State specific venue names and movie times.
Fix a meeting time slightly earlier than the activity start time.

readingPassage.title: Holiday Essay: Trip to Barcelona
readingPassage.text: Last summer, I went to Barcelona with my family for one week. We stayed in a cozy hotel near the beach. Every morning we explored famous sights like Park Güell and Sagrada Família, and in the evening we ate delicious tapas. It was an unforgettable trip!

tips: Use past simple verbs consistently ('went', 'stayed', 'explored', 'ate').
Mention duration, travel companions, and destination clearly.
Add sensory details about food, weather, and landmarks.

topic.title: A restaurant review
topic.description: Read a detailed review analyzing food quality, service, and ambiance at a local bistro.

readingPassage.title: Review: The Riverside Bistro
readingPassage.text: Located by the river, The Riverside Bistro offers a modern European menu with fresh seasonal ingredients. I tried the roasted salmon with asparagus, which was cooked to perfection. The service was attentive, though slightly slow during peak evening hours. Overall, highly recommended for romantic dinners or family celebrations. Rating: 4.5/5.

tips: Combine praise for food quality with balanced observations on service or wait times.
Describe ambiance and specific dishes using vivid adjectives.
End with a clear overall rating and target customer recommendation.

exercises.instruction: Decide if the statements are True or False.

readingPassage.title: Email: Travel Tips for Rome
readingPassage.text:
Hi David,

It's great to hear you're visiting Rome next month! I strongly recommend buying your Colosseum tickets online in advance to skip the long queues. Also, make sure to visit Trastevere for authentic pasta. Don't forget to wear comfortable shoes because you'll do a lot of walking!

Have an amazing trip!
Elena

Provide practical advice regarding booking ahead or footwear.
Include specific food or district suggestions.

topic.title: Describing a bar chart
topic.description: Read a short analytical report describing student transport preferences using bar chart data.

readingPassage.title: Report: Student Transport Preferences
readingPassage.text:
The bar chart illustrates how secondary school students travel to school in 2026. 

According to the chart, the vast majority of students (55%) travel by bus, making it the most popular mode of transport. Walking accounts for 25%, while only 12% come by bicycle. Coming by car represents the smallest proportion at 8%.

In summary, public transport remains the dominant choice among students.

tips: Introduce the chart topic clearly in the opening sentence.
Use data descriptions ('vast majority', 'smallest proportion', 'accounts for').
Group data logically and end with an overall summary trend.

exercises.title: Check your understanding: multiple choice
exercises.instruction: Select the correct percentage from the data report.

questions.question: What percentage of students travel to school by bus?

discussion.question: What mode of transport is most common among students in your city?

topic.title: Describing charts and trends
topic.description: Read a report describing internet usage trends over a five-year period.

readingPassage.title: Report: Global Mobile Internet Trends
readingPassage.text:
The line graph shows changes in mobile internet usage between 2020 and 2025. 

Overall, there was a steady increase in daily mobile data consumption. Usage rose sharply from 2.5 GB per person in 2020 to 6.8 GB in 2023, followed by a gradual rise to 8.5 GB by 2025.

tips: Use trend verbs and adverbs ('rose sharply', 'steady increase', 'gradual rise').
Specify timeframe parameters (between 2020 and 2025).
Highlight significant turning points or milestones.

exercises.title: Check your understanding: true or false
exercises.instruction: Decide if the statements are True or False.

questions.statement: Mobile internet usage experienced a steady increase over the 5-year period.

discussion.question: How has your own daily internet usage changed over the past few years?

topic.title: New Year's resolutions
topic.description: Read a blog post reflecting on personal goals, health habits, and self-improvement.

readingPassage.title: Blog: My Goals for the New Year
readingPassage.text: As the new year begins, I have set three main resolutions. First, I aim to read at least one book every month to expand my knowledge. Second, I plan to reduce screen time by turning off my phone after 9 PM. Finally, I intend to practice mindfulness meditation daily to manage stress.

tips: Use future intent verbs ('I aim to...', 'I plan to...', 'I intend to...').
Structure goals using transition markers ('First', 'Second', 'Finally').
Keep goals realistic and specific.

exercises.title: Check your understanding: gap fill
exercises.instruction: Fill in the missing resolution details.

questions.sentence: The writer plans to turn off their phone after ________ PM.

discussion.question: What is one personal goal or resolution you would like to achieve this year?

topic.title: Reflective writing
topic.description: Read a reflective journal entry analyzing a completed team presentation project.

readingPassage.title: Reflective Journal: Team Presentation Project
readingPassage.text: Looking back on our group presentation last week, I learned a lot about teamwork under pressure. While our slide design was visually appealing, we struggled with time management during the Q&A session. Next time, I will ensure we conduct timed practice runs to improve our time distribution.

tips: Evaluate both successes ('visually appealing') and areas for growth ('struggled with time management').
Use reflective opening markers ('Looking back on...', 'Upon reflection...').
End with specific action plans for future improvement.

exercises.title: Check your understanding: true or false
exercises.instruction: Decide if the statements are True or False.

questions.statement: The writer plans to do timed practice runs for future presentations.

discussion.question: What lesson have you learned from a past group project or presentation experience?
